title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-05-20
body:
Sprint week: 2026-05-13 -> 2026-05-20
Owner: Liam Chen (eng-serving-runtime)
Status: Draft (notes from Thurs sync + async followups)

Quick summary:
- Continued kernel work focused on fused attention and memory allocation fixes; landed a smaller-fused matmul path for sequence lengths <= 512 (PR #884).
- KV cache improvements rolled to staging, observed hit-rate improvement and reduced cache-miss amplification for multi-turn chat workloads.
- Batching scheduler tweaks (adaptive window sizing + conservative tail trimming) increased throughput for mixed-short workloads with modest p95 latency tradeoffs.

What went well
- Kernel: Fused attention micro-optimizations merged to main (PR #884). Initial perf runs on A100 show ~12% reduction in end-to-end tokens/sec for long-seq generation (S:2048) when using the new path due to reduced kernel launch overhead. CPU-side binding fix reduced memcpy overhead for small batches.
- KV cache: Deployed cache eviction tuning + prefix hashing fix to staging. Internal metrics: overall KV hit-rate increased from ~72% -> ~81% for the multi-turn chatbot trace we use (~avg turn length 40 tokens). Average cached-prefix reuse increased by ~1.3x.
- Batching: Adaptive window sizing decreased average batch wait time for 0-32 token requests by ~18%, increasing tokens/sec by ~1.15x on heterogeneous mixes. Tail trimming (limit high-latency tails to max 3 windows) reduced 99th pct latency spikes for bursty traffic.

Metrics (staging, compared to baseline w/ previous release)
- End-to-end latency (short requests <=16 tokens): median -6%, p95 -8%
- Throughput (mixed workload tokens/sec): +15% overall (1.15x)
- KV cache hit-rate: 72% -> 81% (trace: prod-sim-05-12)
- GPU utilization (A100 pools): +4pp average during peak, but 99th pct GPU mem pressure unchanged

Recent releases & PRs
- PR #884: fused matmul + kernel args rework (merged)
- PR #892: KV prefix hashing fix + eviction tuning (in review, awaiting perf CI pass)
- INF-3421: Jira ticket tracking adaptive batching tuning and rollout plan

Notes from Thurs sync (5/20)
- Kernel lead (Aisha): We should gate fused path by seq len and model dims; some older 7B forks see regressions for 1k+ sequence when quantization path is used. Action: add model-config gating (Aisha, due Tues).
- KV (Marta): Cache miss storm reproduced with multi-model routing + autoscale; mitigation queued to reduce concurrent cache warming for new model variants. Action: add short jittered backoff to initial requests (Marta + Ravi, due Fri).
- Batching (Ravi): Scheduler change improved short request latency but increased tail for 512+ sequence bursts in synthetic replay. Action: revert conservative tail trimming param and run longer replay (Ravi, now).

Open blockers / risks
- Perf CI flakiness: several perf runs for PR #892 show non-deterministic regressions on p99; needs deeper flamegraph correlation. (Blocker for rollout to prod).
- Memory fragmentation: kernel-level allocator still occasionally triggers OOM on wide-model inference with KV-heavy workloads; reproducer created but root cause uncertain.
- Multi-model routing + KV: when requests route to cold variants concurrently, cache-warming causes transient latency spikes and increased infra cost. Need throttling logic in routing layer.

Action items (next 7 days)
- Aisha: Add model-config gating for fused path and add unit tests for small dim regressions (due 2026-05-25).
- Marta + Ravi: Implement jittered backoff for first N requests to a new model variant to smooth cache warm; test on staging with prod-sim trace (due 2026-05-22).
- Ethan: Investigate perf CI flakiness for PR #892; collect more flamegraphs and add deterministic seeds to microbench harness (due 2026-05-21).
- Ravi: Run extended replay (48h) for batching changes to measure long-tail behavior and cost impact (start 2026-05-21).
- Team: Prepare rollout checklist for KV tuning (rollout to canary pool size 5% with spike monitors + automated rollback). Owner: Liam (due 2026-05-27).

Notes to self / followups
- Add a short Confluence page summarizing fused-kernel gating rules and model-config knobs — link to kernel doc once ready.
- Coordinate with dedicated infra on expected GPU mem changes when KV hit-rate climbs (ops@redwood).

Appendix (quick debugging traces)
- Reproducer for mem fragmentation: ./tools/repro_mem_frag --model redwood/7B-custom --batch 64 --seq 1024 --kv-enabled
- Perf harness commands used: ./bench/run_microbench --kernel fused --iters 500 --seq 2048

If anything needs to be added to the rollout checklist (alerts, dashboards, exact canary sizing), add comments below or ping in #eng-serving-runtime.

-- Liam
(Notes captured after sync; will convert to final if no major changes)
